family: R96V two-stage communicating condensing gas furnace

sourceRefs.title: Rheem 92-24161-124-08: Installation Instructions for (-)96V Series Two-Stage Communicating Gas Furnaces

likelyCauses: Flame sense rod needs cleaning or is disconnected
Igniter is not working properly or disconnected
Flame is not properly spreading from burner to burner
Loose or shorted wiring between rod and control
Improperly mounted or poorly grounded flame sensor
Burner component or flame pattern issues
Flame sense rod needs cleaning or has loose wiring
Improperly mounted or poorly grounded flame sensor
Burner assembly or combustion door gasket not properly sealed
Electrical short from low voltage to ground
Electrical short from low voltage to common
pressure switch bypassed or welded closed

faultCodes.meaning: Low pressure switch open, inducer on high speed
likelyCauses: Disconnected, blocked, or split pressure switch hoses

C11-S1.instruction: Verify if the manual gas shut-off valve is turned on.

C11-S2.instruction: Check manifold pressure during ignition and observe burner flame spreading.

C11-S3.instruction: Inspect the flame sense rod and its wiring connection.

C11-S4.instruction: Check the igniter operation and its electrical connections.

outcome.summary: Turn the gas valve on.
Replace the burner if flame does not spread properly across all burners.

C11-L3.instruction: Check gas supply or replace valve

outcome.summary: Verify gas supply regulation or escalate for manifold pressure issues.
Clean or replace the flame sense rod and check wire connections and ground.
Replace or reposition the igniter or repair wiring connections.
The furnace control may be malfunctioning and needs replacement.

C12-S1.instruction: Inspect the flame sense rod and wiring connections.

C12-S2.instruction: Clean the flame sense rod and secure wiring.

outcome.summary: Clean or replace the flame sense rod and secure all related wiring connections.

C12-S3.instruction: Check the flame sensor mounting and the furnace ground.

outcome.summary: Replace the flame sense rod, then confirm code 12 clears.

C12-S5.instruction: Reinstall or replace the flame sensor or check ground.

outcome.summary: Reinstall or replace flame sensor and ensure proper furnace grounding.

C13-S1.instruction: Inspect the flame sensor rod for carbon buildup, loose connections, or damaged wiring.

C13-S2.instruction: Clean the flame sense rod and secure any loose wiring connections.

outcome.summary: Cleaned the flame sense rod and secured wiring connections.

C13-S3.instruction: Check the flame sensor and furnace burner compartment for proper grounding and correct mounting.

C13-S4.instruction: Reinstall or replace the flame sensor and ensure the furnace chassis is correctly grounded.

outcome.summary: Reinstalled or replaced the flame sensor and verified ground.

C13-S5.instruction: Inspect the burner assembly components, door gaskets, and seals for proper installation and leaks.

C13-S6.instruction: Ensure proper installation and tight seals between burner and blower compartments, replacing damaged gaskets.

outcome.summary: Repaired and sealed burner compartment gaskets.

C13-S7.instruction: Verify stable burner flame patterns and escalate if flame loss continues despite correct sensor and seals.

outcome.summary: Flame loss persists with proper sensor and seals; further advanced diagnosis required.

C22-S1.instruction: Check for proper blower operation during heat mode.

C22-S2.instruction: Check ductwork, filters, and temperature rise against nameplate values.

C22-S3.instruction: Inspect limit control wiring and connections.

C22-S4.instruction: Check manifold pressure at high fire.

outcome.summary: Check blower motor wiring and replace the blower motor if it fails to run.
Clear airflow restrictions, replace dirty filters, and ensure proper ductwork design.
Repair or replace any loose, broken, or faulty wiring connected to the limit control.
Replace the faulty main limit control after verifying correct airflow and pressures.
Insure properly sized burner orifices are installed and adjust manifold pressure to the nameplate value.

C30-S1.instruction: Inspect low-voltage wiring for shorts to ground or common.

C30-S2.instruction: Repair the short circuit and replace the fuse.

outcome.summary: Repair the short circuit condition and replace the fuse.
Check transformer and secondary wiring integrity.

C33-S1.instruction: Check for obstructions in combustion venting and verify maximum vent lengths.

C33-S2.instruction: Inspect burner assembly components, door seals, and heat exchanger condition.

C33-S3.instruction: Check pressure switches and wiring connections for bypass or faults.

outcome.summary: Remove obstructions in combustion venting and ensure proper terminations.
Replace damaged heat exchanger components or burner assembly parts.
Replace faulty pressure switch or repair any bypassed wiring.
Escalate for advanced diagnostics on rollout limit and burner stability.

C45-S1.instruction: Check the pressure switch hoses for any blocks, splits, cuts, or disconnections.

C45-S2.instruction: Check the inlet and exhaust vent pipes for any blockage or improper termination.

C45-S3.instruction: Inspect the wiring and electrical connections between the control board, inducer, and pressure switch.

C45-S4.instruction: Verify that the inducer motor operates correctly on high speed during pre-purge.

outcome.summary: Replace or reconnect the pressure switch hoses as necessary.
Clear any blockage from the inlet or exhaust vents and repair termination.
Repair or replace faulty wiring and secure loose electrical connections.
Replace the faulty low pressure switch.
Repair or replace the inducer motor, inducer wiring, or control board.

safetyStops.message: Stop. Possible gas leak. Don't operate switches or the furnace. Leave the area, then follow your company's gas leak procedure and call the gas utility.
Stop. Possible carbon monoxide. Get everyone outside to fresh air, leave the furnace off, and call 911 from outside.
Stop. Possible overheating or fire. Shut off power at the disconnect and don't restart until the cause is found and fixed.
Stop. Water near live electrical parts. Shut off power at the disconnect before touching anything and dry the area first.
Stop. Exposed or damaged wiring. Shut off and lock out power before going any further.
Stop. Flame rollout is a fire hazard. Shut off gas and power. Don't reset the rollout switch until the heat exchanger and venting are inspected.
